```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
library(cytoJointR)
# The fit chunks run only where CmdStan is installed.
has_stan <- requireNamespace("cmdstanr", quietly = TRUE) &&
  !is.null(tryCatch(cmdstanr::cmdstan_version(error_on_NA = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL))
```

This vignette runs the whole count workflow on a small simulated data set.
The vocabulary (donor, contrast, pattern, net score, display-only value) is
defined in `GLOSSARY.md` in the package source.
Chunks that need CmdStan run only when it is installed
(`r if (has_stan) "it is here" else "it is not here, so the fit chunks are shown but not run"`).

## Data

`cj_simulate_counts()` draws exact pattern counts from the model the fit
assumes, so the truth is known. Here: 12 donors, three markers, one
stimulation (CMV), two visits, and 20% of the donor-visits have no control
sample.

```{r sim}
sim <- cj_simulate_counts(n_donors = 12, markers = c("IFNG", "TNF", "IL2"),
                          stimulations = "CMV", visits = c("v1", "v2"), N = 1500,
                          missing_control = 0.2, donor_visit = TRUE, seed = 2)
sim$data$provenance$generator
```

The simulator returns a `cj_data`. With your own data, build one with
`cj_from_counts()`. It takes a long table of raw integer counts (one row per
sample and pattern) and a sample table, and it checks both.
`cj_from_events()`, `cj_from_polyicsflow()` and `cj_from_gatingset()` end in
the same constructor. A two-marker example:

```{r from-counts-small}
tab <- data.frame(
  sample_id = rep(c("D1_ctrl", "D1_cmv"), each = 4),
  IFNG = rep(c(0, 1, 0, 1), 2), TNF = rep(c(0, 0, 1, 1), 2),
  count = c(940, 30, 20, 10, 800, 90, 60, 50))
smp <- data.frame(sample_id = c("D1_ctrl", "D1_cmv"), donor_id = "D1",
                  visit = factor("v1"), parent_population = "CD4",
                  condition = c("control", "CMV"))
cj_from_counts(tab, smp, c("IFNG", "TNF"))
```

`summary()` shows donors, visits, stimulations and the contrasts that have no
control sample.

```{r summary}
x <- sim$data
summary(x)
```

## Describe

`cj_describe()` gives counts, percentages and the signed net percent
(stimulated minus control) per contrast and pattern.

```{r describe}
dsc <- cj_describe(x)
head(dsc$patterns[, c("contrast_id", "pattern", "pct_stim", "pct_ctrl", "net_percent")])
head(dsc$at_least)
```

`net_percent` is signed and never clipped. The column `net_percent_display`
is `pmax(net_percent, 0)` and `display_only` marks the rows where the two
differ. Use the clipped column for plots only, never for inference.

```{r clipped}
table(display_only = dsc$patterns$display_only)
```

The plots use the signed values.

```{r describe-plots}
cj_plot_pattern_heatmap(x, contrast = "D01_v1_CD4_CMV")
cj_plot_degree_bars(x, "at_least")
```

The pairwise scatters work from events, not counts.

```{r scatter, message = FALSE}
ev <- cj_simulate_cells(donors = 4, cells_per_sample = 400, seed = 1)$cells
cj_plot_pattern_scatter(ev, c("IFNG", "TNF", "IL2"),
                        c(IFNG = 0, TNF = 0, IL2 = 0), max_cells = 2000)
```

## Fit

`cj_fit()` fits the M1 model in Stan. `centered = TRUE` samples the donor
effects on their natural scale with a dense metric. It gives the same
posterior and is much faster when samples have many cells. The first call
compiles the model, which takes about a minute and is cached.

```{r fit, eval = has_stan, message = FALSE}
fit <- cj_fit(x, centered = TRUE, chains = 4, iter_warmup = 500,
              iter_sampling = 500, seed = 1, adapt_delta = 0.95,
              show_messages = FALSE)
fit
```

## Diagnostics

`print()` reports R-hat, effective sample size, divergences, treedepth hits
and E-BFMI, and warns when one is outside its usual threshold. The full table
is in `fit$diagnostics$summary`. Check this before reading any score.

```{r diagnostics, eval = has_stan}
fit$diagnostics[c("max_rhat", "min_ess_bulk", "n_divergent", "n_max_treedepth")]
head(summary(fit)$table, 8)
```

## Scores

`cj_scores()` evaluates each net score inside every posterior draw: the
stimulated and control probabilities of the same draw are paired, so draws
stay aligned. The scores are `RMS`, `poly_absolute`, `poly_marginal`, `CPS`,
`CCS`, `breadth` and `marker_magnitude`.

Epsilon is the smallest effect you would call meaningful, in the units of the
score. You must choose it before looking at the results; there is no default.
For each score the function returns three probabilities that sum to one:

* `p_positive`: P(score > epsilon), a clear increase over control.
* `p_negative`: P(score < -epsilon), a clear decrease.
* `p_negligible`: P(|score| <= epsilon), no change that matters.

```{r scores, eval = has_stan}
eps <- c(RMS = 0.005, poly_absolute = 0.005, poly_marginal = 0.005, CPS = 0.02,
         CCS = 0.005, breadth = 0.05, marker_magnitude = 0.005)
sc <- cj_scores(fit, eps)
# D08_v1_CD4_CMV has no control sample in this simulation.
sc[sc$score == "RMS" & sc$contrast_id %in% c("D01_v1_CD4_CMV", "D06_v1_CD4_CMV", "D08_v1_CD4_CMV"),
   c("contrast_id", "estimate", "lower", "upper", "p_positive", "p_negative",
     "p_negligible", "status")]
```

Three points about these numbers.

* **Net scores are signed.** A stimulation can lower a score below its
  control. The estimate is then negative and `p_negative` is large. Nothing
  is clipped at zero.
* **Unavailable contrasts.** A donor-visit without a control sample has no
  background, so its net scores cannot be computed. Those rows have
  `status = "unavailable"` and `NA` estimates. They are not zero and not
  dropped. The stimulated sample still enters the fit.
* **Clipped values are display-only.** The clipped column of `cj_describe()`
  exists to draw plots like polyICSFlow's. No score here uses it.

```{r unavailable, eval = has_stan}
table(sc$status)
unique(sc$contrast_id[sc$status == "unavailable"])
```

A draw where the counterfactual solver fails is kept and counted in
`n_failed`, never dropped silently.

## Patterns

`cj_patterns()` splits RMS, CPS or CCS into exact-pattern contributions. They
add up to the global score in every draw. Posterior means add up; interval
bounds do not.

```{r patterns, eval = has_stan}
pt <- cj_patterns(fit, "RMS", c(RMS = 0.005))
head(subset(pt, contrast_id == "D01_v1_CD4_CMV" & status != "unavailable",
            c(pattern, degree, estimate, lower, upper, p_positive)))
```

## Visit change

`cj_visit_change()` subtracts the `from` visit's net score from the `to`
visit's, draw by draw, for each donor. It is `unavailable` for a donor who
lacks a control sample at either visit. The population row averages the
available donors with equal weights and describes these donors only.

```{r visit-change, eval = has_stan}
vc <- cj_visit_change(fit, eps, from = "v1", to = "v2")
subset(vc$population, score == "RMS",
       c(stimulation, estimate, lower, upper, p_positive, n_donors, n_donors_unavailable))
table(vc$donor$reason, useNA = "ifany")
```

## Plots

The response heatmap shows, per donor and pattern, the probability that the
pattern's contribution exceeds epsilon. Unavailable contrasts are left out.
The forest plot shows the signed score per contrast with its interval and the
`+-epsilon` lines; the caption counts the unavailable contrasts.

```{r heatmap, eval = has_stan, fig.height = 4}
cj_plot_response_heatmap(pt, "p_positive")
```

```{r forest, eval = has_stan, fig.height = 5}
cj_plot_forest(sc, score = c("RMS", "CCS"))
```

```{r no-stan, eval = !has_stan, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
cat("*CmdStan was not found, so the chunks that fit the model were not run.",
    "Install it with `cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()` and rebuild.*")
```
